The set update's dry-run locks its rows with the dialect's UPDATE-strength row lock, which this strategy member spells; the node-row lock plan decides whether it is used (#948).
The operation backend builds the set update's locked dry-run from this strategy member; a strategy without it cannot run `updateWhere()` / `compareAndSet()` without writing before validation (#948).

A keyed set write whose row keys exceed the backend bound-value budget splits across statements and counts and locks every part with this strategy member before writing any, so the split write stays all or nothing (#948).

A set update is now a locked dry-run (`previewNodeSetUpdate`, which applies the compare-and-set `expected` predicates) followed by one keyed write (`updateNodeSet`) shared by both verbs, so a validation or uniqueness refusal is raised before any row is written (#948). The compare-and-set write port has no remaining role.

The keyed set write must name the rows it writes: the ids and row tokens a `previewNodeSetUpdate` dry-run returned, written all or nothing (#948). A write without them would be the unvalidated write the change removes.

`UpdateNodeSetParams` is now the keyed write of a set update: it names the exact rows a `previewNodeSetUpdate` dry-run returned (`rows`) instead of a candidate query, so validation runs before the write (#948). The former selection shape is `UpdateWhereNodeSetParams`.
